meta.framing: LOCKED, site-wide: historical symbolic systems with NO demonstrated validity. DESCRIBED, NEVER PRESCRIBED. This file records THAT a text contains a procedure, what KIND, how STRUCTURED, how COMPLETE, and WHERE cited. It contains no recitable formulae, no executable quantities or timings, no drawable templates, and no second-person instruction. Efficacy is never asserted: the tradition CLAIMS, the text SAYS.
meta.livingTraditionPosture: Every tradition in this slice is PRACTISED TODAY by living communities (Ashkenazi and Sephardi Judaism, Hasidism, the Naqshbandiyya and other Sufi turuq, mainstream Sunni piety in al-Ghazali's case). All entries are written as TEXTUAL HISTORY about manuscripts and editions, never as description of what any present-day community does or should do. Where a text is treated by a living community as sacred or as forbidden (Shams al-Ma'arif is both revered and censured in the modern Muslim world), that reception is recorded as reception, not adjudicated.

vocabGapsProposed.why: Abulafia's hokhmat ha-tseruf, Eleazar of Worms's alphabet-gate exegesis, and Islamic ilm al-huruf are all letter-operations that are neither mantra-recitation (the unit is a letter, not a formula) nor visualization. The prior-art inventory flagged this same gap independently; two agents converging on it is the strongest signal in the file.

Construction of a numbered square is a mathematical operation with a documented mathematical literature (Sesiano) that is ONLY THEN consecrated as a talisman. Collapsing it into consecration-of-object loses the fact that the construction rules are provable arithmetic while the talismanic use is not.

vocabGapsProposed.term: ascetic / dietary regimen (fasting, seclusion, sleep restriction)
vocabGapsProposed.why: The Sar-Torah praxis, the Sefer ha-Malbush rite, and Ibn Arabi's khalwa are all built on multi-day dietary and seclusion regimens. Forcing these into 'purification' destroys the harm signal — the prior-art inventory flagged this too.

A bounded period of withdrawal with a staged inner itinerary is its own procedure-type across both halves of this slice (khalwa; Abulafia's hitbodedut; the Sar-Torah enclosure). AUDIT-CORRECTED R1: the enclosure duration was stated here and has been removed — the vocabulary term does not need it.
al-Ghazali's Ihya' 38 sets out a six-station daily audit of the self. It is a procedure with an enumerated sequence and no recitation, visualization or object at all. Nothing in the vocabulary fits.

vocabGapsProposed.term: intention-setting attached to an existing liturgy (kavvanah)
vocabGapsProposed.why: Lurianic kavvanot are not a separate rite: they are a contemplative overlay mapped onto words of a statutory prayer already being said. The vocabulary has no type for 'procedure that modifies another procedure'.

Lurianic prostration on the graves of tzaddikim is neither funerary (the deceased is long buried) nor liminal in the Bardo sense. Closest existing type is funerary/liminal rite, used here under protest.

vocabGapsProposed.term: adjuration of a named intermediary (hashba'a, azima)
vocabGapsProposed.why: Both corpora bind a NAMED angel/spirit by oath. invocation/evocation is used, but it flattens the distinction between petition and legally-framed compulsion, which is exactly the distinction the Sar-Torah and Birhatiya material turns on.

counts.fragmentaryNote: ZERO fragmentary rows in this slice, and that is a substantive finding rather than an oversight. Both halves of this corpus survive through CONTINUOUS COPYING by communities that never stopped reading them — medieval Hebrew manuscripts and Cairo Genizah fragments on one side, an unbroken Arabic manuscript-and-print tradition on the other. The characteristic defect here is not damage but INSTABILITY: fluid macroforms (Hekhalot), divergent recensions (Sefer Hasidim, Shimmush Tehillim, Shams al-Ma'arif), and pseudepigraphic accretion. A grading scheme built for damaged papyri needs a fifth grade — something like 'unstable' or 'plural' — for texts that are complete in every witness and different in each.

procedures.subtype: adjuration of a named angelic intermediary (hashba'a) — vocabGap: 'adjuration of a named intermediary'
procedures.structure: The macroform contains a narrative ascent through seven palaces in which the 'descender to the chariot' is said to present hymns, divine names and 'seals' at each gate to pass its angelic guardians. The unit of the sequence is gate -> presentation -> passage, repeated seven times; the text supplies the narrative frame and the hymnic material but does not set out a single continuous operator's checklist.
procedures.completenessEvidence: PARTIAL, and the incompleteness is structural, not accidental: (a) the corpus survives as what Schafer calls fluid 'macroforms' with no fixed original, so no single witness is the sequence; (b) the material is embedded in first-person narrative and hymn rather than rubric, so the ordering of some elements is inferable only from the story; (c) the texts themselves gate the practice behind purity and worthiness conditions rather than publishing an open method. Evidence for (a) is the repo's own atlas record quoting Schafer's Synopse position; for (c), Swartz's AJS Review study of the purity requirements.
procedures.harmNote: The ascent material is framed by its own texts as dangerous to the unworthy. It is recorded here as late-antique religious literature only.
procedures.repoCoverage: partial — the atlas `technique` field on hekhalot-literature describes adjurations, hymn/name/seal recitation and the guardian-passing structure in one sentence, correctly labelled as historical practice.
procedures.cite: Schafer, Synopse (1981); Scholem, Major Trends in Jewish Mysticism (1941), lecture 2; repo confluence.js record 'hekhalot-literature'.

procedures.subtype: multi-day seclusion and dietary regimen preceding adjuration — vocabGap: 'ascetic / dietary regimen'
procedures.structure: The Sar-Torah praxis section prescribes a bounded preparatory regimen whose STAGE-KINDS are: an ablution stage; an enclosure stage of stated but unreproduced duration; a dietary-restriction stage; and a ritual-purity-avoidance condition. The regimen is enumerated end to end in the text and terminates before the adjuration. STAGE-KINDS ONLY are named here; the durations, the meal pattern, the permitted food and drink classes, the immersion counts and the adjuration formulae are deliberately NOT reproduced. AUDIT-CORRECTED (R33 hostile audit, RAZOR STRIKE R1): the previous wording gave the meal pattern ('a single evening meal') and the sibling row at jew:sar-ha-torah gave the enclosure duration ('the twelve-day enclosure regimen') — both are executable timings on a harm-flagged multi-day fast, and both contradicted this record's own compliance sentence. procedures.completenessEvidence: COMPLETE: the preparatory regimen is one of the few genuinely rubric-shaped passages in the whole corpus — it names each requirement in order and terminates. Schafer collates the variants at SS281-306 in Ubersetzung 2; Swartz's AJS Review article treats the seclusion/fast/ablution/niddah-avoidance sequence as a discrete purity protocol. I grade it complete BECAUSE the text names a terminus (the regimen ends and the adjuration begins) rather than trailing into 'and the rest is known'.
procedures.harmNote: A multi-day enclosed fast with restricted fluid intake is capable of real physical harm. Recorded as the content of a late-antique text; no durations or dietary details are given here and none should be.

procedures.subtype: oath-binding adjuration of the angel called Prince of the Torah, for memory and learning
procedures.structure: A three-part shape: (1) the preparatory purity and seclusion regimen; (2) the adjuration proper, in which a named angelic prince is bound by oath; (3) a claimed result — prodigious memory and mastery of Torah — followed in the tales by the adept transmitting the method onward. The transmission step is itself part of the narrative structure: Swartz notes the tales have the rabbis, once endowed, teach others the formulas.

That is precisely why Swartz can analyse it as a ritual rather than as a myth. Grade is for the SHAPE only; the formulae are not reproduced here.

What is missing is any rubric whatsoever — no sequence, no preparation, no purpose-statement, no result. That absence is verifiable from length and genre alone: the whole text is shorter than a single Hekhalot praxis section, and the repo's own atlas body describes it as 'a terse Hebrew treatise... describing creation'. Every procedure later attached to it arrives in the COMMENTARY tradition, which is why the golem material is filed under Eleazar of Worms below and not here.

procedures.structure: The commentary is the best-known witness to a four-stage shape: (1) selection and preparation of a virgin earth-and-water material; (2) forming of an anthropoid figure; (3) a recitation running through the alphabet-combination 'gates' of Sefer Yetzirah, correlated limb by limb with the figure; (4) in the wider tradition, a reversal or undoing step. STAGES ONLY are named. The gate-sequences, the letter-orders, the site conditions and the reversal are NOT reproduced here and must not be reconstructed from this record.
procedures.completenessEvidence: COMPLETE in the sense that the commentary names every stage from material to animation and does not defer any of them to a teacher — which is exactly why it became the canonical golem source and why Idel devotes a full study to it. Two honest qualifications: (a) the manuscript tradition of the commentary varies, so 'complete' describes the received recension, not a single autograph; (b) Idel and others stress that for Eleazar and many kabbalists the operation was understood as a MYSTICAL EXPERIENCE of creative language, not as the manufacture of a working servant — i.e. the text is complete as a rite and contested as to what the rite was for.
procedures.harmNote: The golem is among the most-appropriated items in Jewish esoterica and a recurring motif in antisemitic caricature. It is admitted here only as textual history of a commentary tradition, with the tradition's own interpretation (a contemplative exercise in creative language) given equal weight to the literal reading.
procedures.repoCoverage: none — the golem tradition appears nowhere in shipped repo data.

procedures.subtype: recitation of the seventy-two-letter Name in permuted forms — vocabGap: 'letter-permutation / gematria contemplation'
procedures.structure: This is the most explicitly procedural text in the Jewish half of the slice, and it is procedural in an unusual way: the METHOD IS THE PAGE LAYOUT. The Braginsky manuscript carries ten large circles in red and black plus 128 smaller circles in black, each circle holding a divine Name broken into letter-combinations; each is described by the collection as detailed instruction for meditation, and each has a marked ENTRY POINT — a pen stroke slightly right of top — telling the reader where the circuit begins. The practitioner works the circle from its entrance while reciting. The procedure is thus: enter at the mark, traverse the combination, recite, proceed to the next figure. NO circle, letter-string, entry-mark or ordering is reproduced here, and none should be reconstructed.
procedures.completenessEvidence: COMPLETE, and unusually so — I grade it complete because (a) the text supplies the material to be recited, (b) it supplies the order, via the physical entry-marks, and (c) it supplies the coordination (breathing and head-movement, per the repo's own atlas record and Idel), leaving no stage explicitly deferred to a teacher. Abulafia wrote as a propagandist for his method and published rather than withheld it. The honest qualification: the manuscripts differ, and Idel's studies are built on collating them, so 'complete' describes the received Braginsky-type recension.
procedures.harmNote: The stated goal is an ecstatic/prophetic state pursued through prolonged recitation with breath control and solitary retreat. Deliberate hyperventilation or breath-holding carries real physical risk, and the technique's own tradition warned that it could unseat the unprepared. Described as 13th-century method; no instructions given.
procedures.repoCoverage: partial — the atlas record on person-abulafia describes hokhmat ha-tseruf (permute, write, vocalize the letters of divine names, coordinated with controlled breathing and prescribed head movements) in one sentence, explicitly as historical method and not instruction. This is one of only two records in the whole repo that comes close to a graded operative description.
procedures.cite: Braginsky Collection, MS 251 catalogue entry (fetched 2026-07-30), citing Idel 1988/1989, Scholem 1961, Wolfson 2000, Sotheby's NY 2004; repo confluence.js record 'person-abulafia'.

procedures.subtype: recitation coordinated with controlled breathing and prescribed head movements

procedures.subtype: construction and consecration of awfaq (magic squares) and lettrist talismans — vocabGap: 'numerical-grid / magic-square construction'
procedures.structure: The printed work runs to roughly forty unnumbered chapters (fasl). Its opening chapters introduce magic squares and the combination of numbers and letters that the text claims produce effect; later material covers talismans and amulets, astrological timing, and planetary correspondences. Al-Buni's Shams is credited in the mathematical literature with setting out general methods for constructing BORDERED magic squares — i.e. the operative core includes genuine constructive mathematics. Chapter counts and the presence of these classes of material are recorded; no construction rule, square, letter-value or consecration wording is reproduced here.
procedures.completenessEvidence: COMPLETE, with a sharp caveat about WHICH text is complete. The printed al-kubra reads as an exhaustive compendium that withholds little — that comprehensiveness is precisely why it became the reference work and why it is also a scholarly problem: the completeness is the SIGNATURE OF ACCRETION, not of authorship. Evidence: three independently circulating pre-print recensions of differing length, ~40 unnumbered chapters in print, and Coulon's anachronism argument. So: complete as a printed compendium; textually unstable; not al-Buni's.
procedures.harmNote: The work is simultaneously revered and censured in the modern Muslim world (its censorship and destruction history is a documented reception phenomenon). Its contents include material aimed at compelling outcomes and binding intermediaries. Admitted here as academic religious history with the ethics note attached, per the repo's abhicara precedent.

procedures.subtype: silent (khafi) dhikr as the order's distinguishing discipline
procedures.structure: Eleven named principles form the frame, each a Persian phrase naming one discipline. Of the eight from Ghijduwani, three bear directly on the operative method: hush dar dam (awareness while breathing), yad-kard (remembrance), yad-dasht (recollection); the rest govern comportment and attention (nazar bar qadam, safar dar watan, khalwat dar anjuman, buz-gasht, nigah-dosht). Baha' al-Din's three additions are all 'pauses' — wuquf-i zamani (temporal), wuquf-i 'adadi (numerical), wuquf-i qalbi (of the heart) — i.e. they specify the TIMING, COUNT and LOCUS of the silent recollection. The names of the principles are recorded; their contents as performed are not.
procedures.completenessEvidence: PARTIAL, on the tradition's own terms and for a reason internal to it: the Naqshbandiyya transmits its method by INITIATIC AUTHORISATION from shaykh to disciple. The eleven principles are a public frame naming what is done; the operative content — how the recollection is held, what is counted, where in the body it is located — is precisely what the initiatic relation supplies. That the last three principles specify timing/count/locus WITHOUT the public texts fixing their values is the structural evidence. Compare the inventory agent's grading of initiation-gated practices as referenced/partial.
procedures.harmNote: This is a living, currently-practised Sufi discipline with millions of adherents. It is described here as the textual and historical record of a rule-set, never as method. No breath, count or locus instruction appears in this record.

procedures.subtype: murabata — a six-station daily discipline of the self — vocabGap: 'self-examination / conscience-audit discipline'
procedures.structure: SIX NAMED STATIONS, in order: musharata (setting conditions with the soul), muraqaba (vigilance), muhasaba (self-examination), mu'aqaba (punishment), mujahada (renewed striving), mu'ataba (censure). The sequence is a closed daily loop — condition-setting at the start, audit at the end, and corrective stations that feed back into the next cycle. Structurally this is the nearest Islamic analogue to Guigo II's four rungs, which the inventory agent graded 'complete' on the same criterion.
procedures.completenessEvidence: COMPLETE, on the strongest available evidence-type in this file: the text ENUMERATES its own stations, names each, orders them, and terminates. Multiple independent publisher/bookseller descriptions of the Islamic Texts Society translation give the identical six-item list in the identical order, which is a reliable indicator that the enumeration is the book's own and not a summariser's imposition. No content of any station is reproduced here — only that there are six, and what each is called.
procedures.harmNote: The fourth station is self-imposed 'punishment' (mu'aqaba). Medieval ascetic penance is documented here as textual history with the hazard named; no content is given. The living-tradition flag matters especially here: the Ihya' is a mainstream devotional work read by ordinary Muslims, not occult literature, and must not be filed as though it were.

procedures.subtype: the khalwa itinerary — a staged ascent through what is disclosed in retreat — vocabGap: 'retreat / seclusion discipline'
procedures.structure: A letter, not a rulebook. Its architecture is an ITINERARY OF DISCLOSURES: Ibn 'Arabi describes, in order, what the retreatant will be shown at successive stages and — crucially — what must be refused at each. The organising move of the treatise is warning against arrest at any station, so the sequence is defined negatively as much as positively. English rendering as 'A Sufi Manual on Retreat' is the modern publisher's framing.
procedures.completenessEvidence: PARTIAL, on three converging grounds: (a) the genre is an epistle to ONE named senior disciple, so it assumes that disciple's formation and states it does not supply; (b) it describes what is disclosed rather than prescribing what is done — the practical conditions of khalwa (duration, fasting, seclusion arrangements, the shaykh's supervision) are presupposed from the Sufi milieu, not laid out; (c) the treatise's own premise is that the retreat is undertaken UNDER AUTHORISATION. Compare the inventory agent's grading of Ignatius's Exercises as partial for the identical reason ('under a director').
procedures.harmNote: The tradition and the translation literature both describe khalwa as an ADVANCED AND POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS practice: extended solitude with food and sleep restriction, undertaken in expectation of visionary disclosure. That combination is a documented route to psychological destabilisation. Recorded as 13th-century textual history; the treatise's own warnings are part of what makes it a historical document worth recording.

notes.twoFieldDiscipline: Following the inventory agent, every procedure row carries `textCompleteness` (the source text's own) and `repoCoverage` (what this repo currently records). Across 47 rows, repoCoverage is 'none' for 40, 'partial' for 6, and 'complete-ish' for 1 (picatrix-prayers.js).
